reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading is accurate: line 328 accesses cell_proofs[i * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB + j] without bounds validation. However, this finding is DISPUTED per bug bounty scope rules. The 01e property (outputs/01e_PARTIAL_W3B4_1771748827.json, line 699-715) explicitly marks this as attacker_controlled=false, bug_bounty_scope=conditional, and bug_bounty_eligible=false. The property requires 'Proof slicing indices in cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction must always be within blobs_bundle.proofs bounds' but only for semi-trusted Engine API paths. Phase 03 claims the REST API path (/eth/v2/beacon/blocks) is exploitable, but BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json explicitly excludes Beacon API under out_of_scope.components with reason 'Vulnerabilities requiring the user to have publicly exposed an API, such as the Beacon API, are explicitly out-of-scope'. All three call sites analyzed: (1) REST API rest_beacon_api.nim:1108 - OUT OF SCOPE per program rules; (2) EL recovery nimbus_beacon_node.nim:2054 - semi-trusted Engine API; (3) Validator beacon_validators.nim:587 - semi-trusted Engine API. The two in-scope paths (EL) are semi-trusted boundaries where a compromised local EL is required, making this conditional/latent, not a direct external attack. Per 01e authoritative spec, this is by-design trust boundary differentiation.
